text:
Alex W: Heads up — eu-west GA is reporting ~30% available GPU capacity. Automated traffic shift started ~1h ago but we’re seeing 5xx/502 spikes for some customers that resolve via CNAMEs. Investigating DNS/resolver behaviour.

Jin (SRE): Is this looking like provider-level anycast cache staleness or a mis-tuned TTL? Any recent DNS changes?

Maria - NetOps: We changed default service TTLs from 60 -> 300 last week to reduce auth queries. That probably slowed failover. Rolling a revert for routing records now (300 -> 60 -> 30 for critical). Making changes in cloud-dns console.

Alex W: Copy. Important: do NOT touch apex NS glue. Only A/CNAME/weighted records and healthchecks. If recursive resolvers are sticky with negative caches, we may need weighted endpoints + edge redirects.

Sam - Oncall: ops-bot: run `dig +trace customer.example.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8` and paste output.

ops-bot: `dig +trace customer.example.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8` -> shows stale A records pointing at edge1.eu-west.redwood.ai TTL=120 still being served from 8.8.8.8. Authoritative NS list points at ns1-cloudprovider.net. No zone transfer errors.

Jin (SRE): Plan: 1) temporarily lower TTLs to 30 on failover/routing records; 2) create weighted records where eu-west -> eu-central fallback with higher weight; 3) actively prime public resolvers from multiple vantage points (dig from EC2, GCP, DO); 4) if resolvers still hold old entries, open provider cache-flush ticket.

Maria - NetOps: Done: lowered `api.redwood.ai` and `*.svc.redwood.ai` TTL -> 30. Push is live but propagation will vary — some resolvers ignore <60. Note logged change id `dns-change-334`.

Sam - Oncall: Triggering traffic-shift runbook: `curl -s -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/api/traffic-shift" -d '{"from":"eu-west","to":"eu-central","pct":40}'` — job queued. Watching error rates.

ops-bot: traffic-shift job 872 queued, ETA ~18s. eu-central GPU headroom +12% (autoscaler reports).

Alex W: Keep cost in mind — cross-region traffic increases egress and instance-hours. For customers with reserved capacity in eu-west, notify account teams before extended shift.

Jin (SRE): Early signs: routed pool 502s down by ~60%, but some clients still hit old IPs. Sam, run the priming script from synthetic runners across ISPs to warm/evict caches.

Sam - Oncall: Ran priming loop. Snippet results: `resolver=1.1.1.1 host=api.redwood.ai resolved=10.2.3.4 TTL=6 (expired)`, `resolver=ISP-A host=api.redwood.ai resolved=10.2.3.4 TTL=120 provider=ISP-A (stale)`. Several ISPs appear to ignore short TTLs.

Maria - NetOps: Opened support case with provider-NET (#NET-2201): requested anycast cache clear + help priming authoritative nodes. Also added temporary HTTP 302 redirect at old edge host -> fallback hostname to catch stuck clients.

Alex W: Post-incident actions: revert TTLs to 300 after stable, document which ISPs ignore sub-60 TTLs, quantify cost delta for cross-region compute/egress during shift, and update runbook to include DNS-weighting + edge-redirect pattern for faster customer-visible failover.

Jin (SRE): Runbook note: prefer short-lived weighted records + `surrogate-control` on redirects. Avoid changing apex glue. Include explicit steps for provider cache flush and sample `dig` commands to validate.

Sam - Oncall: :thumbsup: error rates returned to baseline on routed pool. Will close loop in 30m and file postmortem with timelines and cost estimate.
